rule: One multi-cell shape of colour A plus a lattice (spacing 2) of single dots: one A centre dot, the rest colour B. Output: the shape stays in place recoloured B. Each B dot at offset (2uy,2ux) from the centre adds an A copy of the shape shifted by (uy*h, ux*w), where h x w is the shape's bounding box. Dots are erased and copies are clipped at the border.
scope: Dot-constellation offsets control copies of a connected shape at multiples of its bounding-box dimensions. Original shape swaps to the dot colour, copies retain its old colour, and dots disappear. Optional clipped copies retain at least half their cells.
constraints: All four canonical pairs reconstruct exactly and contain no clipping; the archived prose claim about pair3 clipping is contradicted by the actual grids.

authored_scope: Supported: grids 12..30 per side by default, including rectangular ones (explicit sizes 1..30 are accepted if feasible); random 4-connected non-full masks in 2..4 x 2..4 boxes; explicit masks of any size; 1..5 random B dots (up to 24 via num_dots) in an 8-connected cluster within +-2 lattice units; explicit offsets with gcd 1; random distinct colours, any subset of which may be fixed. Clipping is a labelled synthetic extension because no canonical pair clips; the reference prose about pair 3 clipping is wrong. The clipping mode (clip / noclip / any) is resolved once per call. With defaults it is a single 15% draw for forced clipping, and placement is enumerated under that mode. force_clip=True never yields an unclipped scene; it raises ValueError instead. Not supported: multiple shapes, dot spacing other than 2, copies keeping fewer than half their cells, dots touching the shape box, overlapping copies.
authored_constraints: Exactly one A-coloured single-cell dot (the centre) and at least one B dot
Gcd of the unit offsets is 1, so the pixel dot spacing is exactly 2
Shape mask is 4-connected, touches every row and column of its box, and has at least 2 cells (3 for random masks, never a full rectangle)
No dot lies inside the shape bounding box or the one-cell ring around it
bg, A and B are distinct; bg is strictly the most frequent input colour
Copy boxes are distinct nonzero multiples of (h,w), so they never overlap each other or the original
In clip mode at least one copy is clipped; in noclip mode none is; every clipped copy keeps at least half its cells
Explicit shape_pos and centre outside the grid are rejected before any retry loop
Output always differs from the input: the shape is recoloured, dots are erased and copies are added
